execution_environment.note: All decisions were obtained by feeding the real hook a PreToolUse JSON payload on stdin and reading .hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision; exit code 2 was mapped to 'deny' (deny() exits 2 and emits no JSON).

fail_reasons: security 3 < 7 (critical tier) — automatic fail regardless of other dimensions
28 lab-confirmed control-plane destructions are decided 'allow' by the hook, on a surface where the detection/recovery layer provides zero coverage
what_this_commit_got_right: Claim 1 is TRUE and independently reproduced. All 45 counterexamples from the 11th verdict's full_bypass_list_45 are now blocked (ask/deny): 45/45 on bash 5.3 AND 45/45 on bash 3.2. The unified __tokenize_segment() backslash model is correct.

Claim 3 is TRUE and independently reproduced. tests/pre-bash-firewall.bats 284/284 (0 failures). Full tests/ suite: plan line '1..849'; I observed 750 consecutive passes before a harness timeout, then ran the 9 remaining files to completion for 110/110. Zero 'not ok' lines anywhere across both runs.

The fail-closed machinery is real and I verified it end-to-end, not by reading: unclosed double quote, unclosed single quote, unterminated backtick, unbalanced paren inside $() (rm -rf $(echo "(") .claude), ANSI-C quoting $'.claude', locale quoting $".claude", and the >2048-char length cap ALL return ask.
Hook is robust to malformed input: empty tool_input and non-JSON stdin both exit 0 without crashing.
The tokenizer consolidation is good engineering — one state machine instead of two divergent scanners, with the bash 3.2 empty-array and quadratic-substring pitfalls documented from measurement.
issues: [security][critical][confidence:high] 28 command forms that REALLY DESTROY the control plane are decided 'allow'. The delete verb is written LITERALLY inside a command substitution, where __tokenize_segment() skips the construct's contents wholesale, so no literal verb token ever reaches the segment and armed stays 0 — which means the SEGMENT_HAS_OPAQUE flag introduced by this commit is never consulted. Verbs: mv (12), find -delete (12), rmdir (4). Targets: .claude (8), .claude/hooks (8), .claude/plugins (12).

[security][critical][confidence:high] The compensating control this commit relies on DOES NOT EXIST as described. Layer 2 INDIRECT_PATTERNS matches only \b(rm|chmod|chown|mkfs|eval)\b inside $(...) and backticks. scan_control_plane_delete() arms on rm|rmdir|unlink|shred|mv|find. Five of those six verbs are absent from Layer 2's alternation, and 'rmdir' is not even reached by \brm\b (no word boundary before 'dir'). So the premise 'literal dangerous verb inside a substitution is already denied by Layer 2' is false for mv, rmdir, unlink, shred and find.

[security][critical][confidence:high] The newly declared residual risk verb_via_substitution MISDESCRIBES the gap it declares. Its 'compensating' field states the remaining set is only verbs encoded to evade literal matching (hex/base64). Every one of my 28 counterexamples uses a plain literal verb name and is still allowed. The declaration therefore understates the open axis from 'encoded verbs only' to 'every delete verb except rm', which is the difference between an accepted principled limit and an unknown hole.

[security][critical][confidence:high] docs/INVARIANTS.md repeats the same false claim verbatim ('남는 몫은 동사 자체가 통째로 치환 안에 숨어 있고(리터럴 대조도 피하도록 hex/base64 등으로 인코딩) ... 경우뿐이다'). A future round reading INVARIANTS.md will believe this axis is closed except for encoding tricks and will not re-test it.

[security][high][confidence:high] There is no post-hoc safety net on this surface. .claude/ is listed in .gitignore, `git ls-files .claude` returns 0 tracked files, and PROTECTED_GLOBS in hooks/protected-integrity.sh contains no .claude entry. Recovery is `git checkout HEAD -- <path>`, which cannot restore untracked/ignored content. The hook's own header comment (lines 20-22) already names this exact condition as 'the place where prediction is the only means'. The 28 bypasses land precisely there.

[security][medium][confidence:high] The path-specific ASK arms that incidentally catch some of these are defeated by targeting the parent directory. `mv .claude/settings.json /tmp/s` inside a backtick asks (arm: cp/mv on settings paths), but `mv .claude /tmp/s` inside a backtick is allowed — and it destroys settings.json anyway. Enumerating child paths while leaving the containing directory open is not a partial mitigation, it is a no-op against an adversary.

[error][high][confidence:high] The commit states a fail-closed principle ('구문을 확실히 이해 못 하면 무장 여부와 무관하게 즉시 ask') and then carves out the one construct where the scanner deliberately does not read the contents. For unarmed segments the opaque signal is computed and then discarded. That is an 'unknown treated as safe' path inside a policy whose stated rule is 'unknown is unsafe'.

[test][high][confidence:high] The two new substitution tests encode the false premise instead of testing it. 'command substitution inside an armed segment still asks' uses only rm/mv with a LITERAL verb outside the substitution; 'command substitution with no delete verb stays frictionless' uses only genuinely benign commands (git commit, ls $(pwd), echo date). The decisive middle case — a non-rm delete verb literally INSIDE the substitution — is not tested, which is exactly why 284/284 is green while 28 destructive forms are allowed.

[test][medium][confidence:high] No test asserts consistency between Layer 2's substitution verb alternation and scan_control_plane_delete()'s arming verb list. These two lists are the load-bearing halves of this commit's safety argument and they are free to drift silently. A single parity test over the two verb sets would have caught this before commit.

[quality][medium][confidence:medium] __skip_dollar_paren() counts parens without tracking quotes, which the comment acknowledges. I probed the two directions and both currently fail closed (rm -rf $(echo "(") .claude -> ask via unmatched-depth; rm -rf $(echo ")") .claude -> ask via trailing unclosed quote). Not a live defect, but the safety here is incidental to two other checks rather than a property of this function.

[quality][low][confidence:high] The commit message, INVARIANTS.md and the contract all assert '849/849' as a single measured figure. It is correct, but 284 of those are the firewall suite whose green status is precisely what failed to detect this class — the number is being used rhetorically as evidence of safety when it is evidence of suite coverage.

counterexamples._how_to_reproduce: For each command C: (1) decision = jq -n --arg c "$C" '{tool_name:"Bash",tool_input:{command:$c}}' | CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=<repo> bash hooks/pre-bash-firewall.sh, read .hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision (exit 2 == deny). (2) ground truth = build a lab dir containing .claude/{settings.json,settings.local.json,hooks/guard.sh,plugins/}, hooks/hooks.json, progress/feature_list.json; cd into it; run the command with a real shell; assert every one of those artifacts still exists.
counterexamples._measured_on: hook executed under bash 5.3 and bash 3.2 (identical results); destruction executed under /bin/bash 3.2, /usr/local/bin/bash 5.3 and /usr/local/bin/zsh (identical results)
counterexamples._result: 120 candidates generated (5 targets x 6 payloads x 4 wrappers). 28 are 'allow' AND destroy the control plane. 0 false alarms in the other direction.
counterexamples._severity_caveat_stated_honestly: 24 of the 28 (the mv and find -delete forms) are unconditionally destructive: mv relocates the whole tree, find -delete removes it depth-first. The remaining 4 (rmdir .claude/plugins) only succeed when that directory is empty, as it was in my lab; on a real install with plugins present rmdir would fail. The security conclusion rests on the 24, not on the rmdir subset.
counterexamples._regression_status: NOT a regression introduced by this commit. Parent 6085b80 allows all 28 as well. This is a pre-existing hole that this commit's rationale newly and incorrectly claims is covered.
counterexamples._counterfactual: I patched HEAD's tokenizer to set SEGMENT_UNSAFE unconditionally on backtick/$( (a 4-line sed, i.e. the 11th-verdict design the commit backed out of). That version blocks 28/28 of these. It also turns 5 of 12 ordinary commands from allow to ask (git commit with backticks, ls $(pwd), echo `date`, for f in $(ls), grep -r "$(whoami)"). So the rescoping is a genuine trade, but it was made on a false model of what Layer 2 covers, and the forfeited coverage is 28 destructive forms rather than the 'hex/base64-encoded verbs' the declaration claims.

layer2_gap_proof.scan_control_plane_delete_arming_verbs: rm, rmdir, unlink, shred, mv, find(-delete)
layer2_gap_proof.observed: `rm -rf .claude` -> deny (Layer 2 fires). `mv .claude /tmp/x` in backticks -> allow. `rmdir .claude/hooks` in backticks -> allow. `find .claude -delete` in backticks -> allow.
layer2_gap_proof.partial_incidental_coverage: unlink/shred against .claude/settings.json and hooks/hooks.json ask via a separate literal ASK arm \b(rm|unlink|shred)\b[^;|&]*(hooks/hooks\.json|\.claude/settings(\.local)?\.json). That arm is path-enumerated and is bypassed by naming the parent directory.

convergence_judgment.assessment: Real progress on the axis under review, but the round does not converge. The backslash/tokenizer work is correct and I confirmed it independently; the failure is not in the tokenizer but in the safety argument used to justify the one carve-out the commit added on top of it.
convergence_judgment.pattern_across_rounds: This is the fifth consecutive round in which a verb-name or pattern list is used as a security boundary and the list turns out to be incomplete. Round 10 removed a verb-substring pre-filter for exactly this reason ('동사 이름을 사전 필터로 쓰지 않는다'); this round reintroduces dependence on a verb list — Layer 2's rm|chmod|chown|mkfs|eval — one layer further down, and it fails the same way. The lesson recorded after round 10 was not applied to the layer being leaned on.
convergence_judgment.why_the_suite_did_not_catch_it: The two new tests probe the two endpoints the author was reasoning about (armed segment with substitution; benign command with substitution) and not the midpoint that the rationale asserts is covered. Tests written to confirm a rationale cannot falsify it.

recommendation.primary: Do not treat 'a verb appears literally inside a substitution' as covered until the two verb lists are unified. Either (a) extend Layer 2's substitution alternation to the full arming set (rm|rmdir|unlink|shred|mv|find), or (b) let SEGMENT_HAS_OPAQUE arm the segment when the skipped substitution's raw text contains any arming verb, or (c) revert to unconditional ask for substitutions and buy the friction back with a narrow allowlist for substitutions that contain no arming verb at all. (b) is closest to the commit's existing structure and does not reopen the friction the rescoping fixed.
recommendation.then: Add a parity test asserting that Layer 2's substitution verb set is a superset of scan_control_plane_delete()'s arming verb set, so the two cannot drift again.
recommendation.also: Correct the verb_via_substitution 'compensating' text and the matching INVARIANTS.md paragraph. As written they will cause a future round to skip re-testing this axis.
recommendation.consider: Independently of the firewall fix, .claude/ has neither prediction coverage (this hole) nor recovery coverage (gitignored, absent from PROTECTED_GLOBS). Whether that surface should get a recovery path at all is a separate design question worth raising with the user, since F65's thesis is that detection/recovery replaces prediction — on this path neither exists.

missing_criteria: No acceptance criterion requires that the delete-verb set used for arming and the delete-verb set used by Layer 2's indirect-execution patterns be consistent, even though the safety argument for the substitution rescoping depends entirely on that consistency.

No criterion requires that a newly declared open_axis be accompanied by a counterexample demonstrating the axis boundary — the verb_via_substitution declaration would have been falsified immediately by one.
ambiguous_criteria: 'compensating' fields in open_axes_2026_08_04 are prose assertions with no executable check. Two of them now assert controls that measurably do not hold.
security_criteria_insufficient: For a critical-tier feature there is no criterion requiring differential (decision vs. real-execution) verification before commit. The implementer's own 284/284 and 849/849 were true and still consistent with 28 live destructive bypasses.
criteria_gaps.action_required: implementer should add the verb-set parity criterion to evals/acceptance-criteria.json and correct the two false compensating-control statements in progress/contracts/sprint-51.json and docs/INVARIANTS.md in the next iteration.

note_for_main_loop: passes remains false for F65. Because the verdict is fail, the F37 critical-tier second independent judgment and the security-auditor dispatch are NOT triggered by this round — they become required only once a round reaches a pass verdict. If a future round does pass, F65 is critical tier and needs BOTH the independent second judge (dispatched in a separate context; verdict disagreement -> human escalation, never auto-pass) AND security-auditor before passes may be set. Note for the next implementation round: the fix here is small and structural (unify two verb lists, or let the skipped substitution's raw text arm the segment) — the tokenizer work from this commit is sound and should be kept, not reverted. Also worth surfacing to the user directly: .claude/ currently has neither prediction nor recovery coverage, which is a design question larger than this bug.
